1.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Engineering] What point does the professor stress about how the inquiry did its work?

options.A: It put gauges in the ground instead of relying on witnesses' recollections
options.B: It heard the laborers who laid the mains as experts rather than as suspects
options.C: It ran for years longer than planned, outlasting the public anger that launched it
options.D: It tested pipe in the yard under conditions the buried network did not face

2.stem: [Academic Talk — Textile Conservation] Why does the professor describe the treatment the banner received in 1968?

options.A: Its adhesive is what the current team must now find a way to remove
options.B: Its photographs preserve details of the border that have since been lost
options.C: It was admired in its day, which shows how quickly conservation standards move
options.D: Its written records let the team date when the discoloration began

3.stem: [Academic Talk — Primatology] What does the professor emphasize about the limits of the follow data?

options.A: Habituation was uneven, so the shyest groups are thinnest in the record
options.B: The two field seasons fell in different fruiting years, muddying the feeding records
options.C: The ear notches used to identify individuals had faded by the second season
options.D: One team could shadow one group at a time, so comparisons rest on different days

4.stem: [Academic Talk — Textile Conservation] What is the professor's position on the museum's decision to send the banner back to the parish?

options.A: He declines to take a side, because his own lab advised the museum in the dispute
options.B: He supports it, since the parish has agreed to display it for part of each year
options.C: He considers the question settled by the loan agreement, whatever anyone's preference
options.D: He opposes it, because the church building stays damp for much of the winter

5.stem: [Academic Talk — Primatology] According to the professor, how did the monkeys' use of the sleeping cliffs change after the road opened?

options.A: They crowded onto a single cliff instead of rotating among several
options.B: They left the cliffs altogether and began sleeping in the forest canopy
options.C: They abandoned the cliff nearest the road while keeping the more distant ones
options.D: They went on using the same cliffs but began arriving after dark

6.stem: [Academic Talk — Sociology] According to the professor, what did Madariaga conclude about how the market's best positions were allocated?

options.A: They rotated through a yearly draw the traders organized themselves
options.B: They changed hands through favors that the fee books do not record
options.C: They passed within families, often across two or three generations
options.D: They followed a seniority order that was understood rather than written down

7.stem: [Academic Talk — Botany] How does the professor judge the agency report that attributed the changes to warming?

options.A: Right about the crest, though drainage work better explains the valley section
options.B: Broadly correct, and if anything too cautious about the pace of change
options.C: Premature, since the area's grazing history could produce the same patterns
options.D: Overstated, because it treats the patchy early records as if they were complete

8.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Mathematics] How does the professor respond to Odile's argument that Dole's shortcut breaks down on steep ground?

options.A: He counters that her surviving hill surveys check out against modern measurements
options.B: He accepts it, noting the notebooks themselves flag the hill pages as unreliable
options.C: He objects that it holds her to a standard no method of the period could meet
options.D: He grants the mathematics but doubts any commission would have used the shortcut there

9.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Mathematics] Why does the professor bring up the toll ledgers of the navigation company?

options.A: They record her buying instruments that go unmentioned in her own pages
options.B: They show Dole was paid for computation, not merely for measuring in the field
options.C: They locate her on the eastern line, far from where the notebooks later surfaced
options.D: They are nearly all that survived the fire in the company's offices

10.stem: [Academic Talk — Folklore Studies] What did the comparison of Ovel's cylinders with her notebooks show?

options.A: Two singers she listed separately turn out to be a single voice on the wax
options.B: The notebook texts were rewritten after the fact into more standard language
options.C: Many songs entered in the notebooks were not recorded at all
options.D: The wax preserves refrains that the written texts leave out

11.stem: [Academic Talk — Textile Conservation] According to the professor, what did the trial cleaning of one corner show?

options.A: The stains lifted unevenly, leaving that corner blotchier than before
options.B: The water itself left a tide line that took a second pass to clear
options.C: The grime had been shielding the fabric beneath, which tested stronger than exposed cloth
options.D: The cleaned corner dried noticeably stiffer than the surrounding weave

12.stem: [Academic Talk — Sociology] Why does the professor talk about the months Madariaga spent running a stall of his own?

options.A: It accounts for a long gap in his field notes that puzzled later readers
options.B: It is where, in the professor's view, his account begins to lose its distance
options.C: It gave him a view of the pre-dawn dealing that outside observers rarely see
options.D: It won him a standing with the traders' committee that interviews had not

13.stem: [Academic Talk — Botany] What does the professor say the resurvey found about the stone daisy?

options.A: The plants were larger on average but flowering much less often
options.B: It persisted on the ledges but had disappeared from the loose rock between them
options.C: It had shifted upslope by far less than the regional models predicted
options.D: Seedlings appeared throughout the transect, yet mature plants were no more numerous

14.stem: [Academic Talk — Folklore Studies] What is the professor's main point about the valley's winter singing evenings?

options.A: They were a recent revival, younger than the collector supposed
options.B: They took up printed song sheets as readily as the older ballads
options.C: They kept the ballads alive after emigration had emptied the villages
options.D: They smoothed away differences between versions once sung farm to farm

15.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Engineering] What does the professor say the inquiry's tests identified as the cause of the bursts?

options.A: The pipes had been laid on filled ground that kept settling beneath them
options.B: Pressure surges from the new pumping engines were splitting sound pipe
options.C: Frost was reaching below the depth the trench specifications assumed
options.D: The failures traced back to a single flawed casting run at the foundry

16.stem: [Academic Talk — Folklore Studies] How does the professor view the archive's decision to put the cylinders online?

options.A: She points out that the singers' descendants asked for the release, which recasts the debate
options.B: She defends it, pointing to the publication terms in Ovel's own agreements
options.C: She thinks the cylinders' physical condition matters more than the argument over permission
options.D: She faults the archive for treating the recordings as the collector's property alone

17.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Engineering] What does the professor suggest became of the inquiry's recommendations?

options.A: They entered the municipal codes but were seldom enforced in practice
options.B: The shift to steel mains made most of them obsolete within a decade
options.C: New districts were built to the rules while the original network was left as it was
options.D: Cities abroad adopted them years before any at home did

18.stem: [Academic Talk — Oceanography] How does the professor respond to the idea that the deep current supplies nutrients to the shelf waters?

options.A: She credits the shelf's nutrients to river runoff instead, whatever the deep water carries
options.B: She doubts it, since the water has shed most of its nutrient load before it gets there
options.C: She finds it convincing, mainly because the sediment traps fill fastest when the flow arrives
options.D: She accepts it, though on the strength of the plankton counts rather than the sediment traps

19.stem: [Academic Talk — Primatology] What does the professor say the forestry department did after the findings were reported?

options.A: It commissioned a second survey rather than acting on the first
options.B: It planted a screen of fast-growing trees along the exposed roadcut
options.C: It closed the road to nighttime traffic during the birth season
options.D: It designated the ridge a reserve while leaving the road itself open

20.stem: [Academic Talk — Textile Conservation] What did the fiber and dye analysis reveal about the banner's red areas?

options.A: Two different red dyestuffs, evidence of a repair campaign long after the banner was made
options.B: The red had shifted from a deeper purple, altering how the design now reads
options.C: The red was painted onto the woven surface rather than dyed into the thread
options.D: A dye tied to workshops well to the north of where the banner was used

21.stem: [Academic Talk — Sociology] How does the professor treat Bahn's objection that the study overlooked the traveling vendors?

options.A: She concedes the omission but argues those vendors had no say in the matters at issue
options.B: She agrees with it and thinks it undermines the study's central claim
options.C: She rejects it, since Bahn's list of vendors dates from years after the study closed
options.D: She counters that Madariaga's own census sheets show he counted them week by week

22.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Engineering] Why does the professor bring up the rival water company across the river?

options.A: Its engineers sat on the panel, a choice that colored how the findings were received
options.B: The rivalry over rates explains why the city refused to fund repairs for so long
options.C: Its eventual purchase of the works ended the dispute without resolving it
options.D: Its takeover bid was what finally pushed the inquiry's report into print

23.stem: [Academic Talk — Oceanography] Why does the professor mention the logbooks kept by the local fishing crews?

options.A: Their catch records offered an independent check on the temperature data
options.B: They show the crews knew the pattern long before an instrument recorded it
options.C: They fixed the date of an equipment failure the team could not otherwise explain
options.D: Their notes on lost gear were what first drew researchers to the site

24.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Mathematics] What evidence does the professor say helped date the notebooks?

options.A: A binding that turned out to be far later than the pages it holds
options.B: A remark about a bridge that was not begun until 1741
options.C: Watermarks showing the paper was made a decade before the earliest entries
options.D: Ink differences showing the entries were added in three separate campaigns

25.stem: [Academic Talk — Oceanography] What does the professor say the instruments in the Danholt Trough recorded about the deep current?

options.A: It grew gradually weaker from one year of the record to the next
options.B: It held steady year-round, apart from brief pulses lasting a few days
options.C: It reversed direction for several weeks in each year of the record
options.D: It ran strongest in the winter months and slackened through each summer

26.stem: [Academic Talk — Botany] Why does the professor discuss the photographs the original surveyor took?

options.A: They let the team find plots whose corner markers had long since vanished
options.B: They show the surveyor's party trampling the very ledges being measured
options.C: They record the old snowbeds, giving a baseline the written notes lack
options.D: They were taken late in the season, which limits what the comparison can claim

27.stem: [Academic Talk — Primatology] What does the professor think of her colleague's suggestion that the change was a response to predators?

options.A: It has more evidence behind it than any of the rival explanations
options.B: It fits the first season's observations but not what the groups did later
options.C: It was developed for open-country species and transfers poorly to forest
options.D: It mistakes an effect of the disturbance for the cause of the change

28.stem: [Academic Talk — Oceanography] What will the research team most likely do next?

options.A: Pair the seafloor measurements with a ship survey each spring
options.B: Release the full measurement series for outside groups to analyze
options.C: Keep the array in place for another two-year deployment
options.D: Shift some of the moorings closer to the edge of the shelf

29.stem: [Academic Talk — Botany] What does the professor imply about the transect's future?

options.A: The next resurvey will wait a full generation, as the original design intended
options.B: A proposed cable-car corridor could cut across the plots before the next visit
options.C: The national park will fold the resurvey into its regular monitoring cycle
options.D: With the grant ending, trained volunteers will carry the work forward

30.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Mathematics] According to the professor, what happened to the notebooks after Dole's death?

options.A: They were divided, and half the pages are now in a collection abroad
options.B: They stayed in the family, unread, until a descendant offered them for sale
options.C: They lay misfiled among parish tax rolls until the 1950s
options.D: They passed to a schoolmaster who taught from them for thirty years

31.stem: [Academic Talk — Sociology] What does the professor suggest the market's move to the new hall demonstrated?

options.A: The disputes once settled internally began landing in the municipal courts
options.B: The old order reasserted itself in the new building within a single season
options.C: The city's assigned layout held, at the cost of driving longtime traders out
options.D: Much of the trade skipped the move and resettled in the surrounding streets

32.stem: [Academic Talk — Folklore Studies] Why does the professor mention the customs post at the mouth of the valley?

options.A: Its ledgers show how often the valley's singers actually traveled outside
options.B: It marked the line beyond which a different ballad stock took over
options.C: Its daybook fixes the date of her second visit, which her diary leaves out
options.D: Its officers were among the first people Ovel persuaded to sing for her
